All couplings have the same weighted first moment. Continuous convex tests follow by polygonal approximation from affine functions and nonnegative calls. A finite convex function on a closed interval has finite one-sided limits and only possible upward endpoint jumps. Scaled calls and reflected calls converge boundedly to the respective endpoint indicators.

The cumulative mass of an a_i-bounded marginal is continuous and a_i-Lipschitz and takes value u at the generalized inverse for interior mass levels. Hence the weighted quantile has expansion at least Σλ_i/a_i. Inverse images of intervals satisfy the length bound, which extends to Borel sets by interval covers.

Constant densities on intervals of lengths m/a_i force the reciprocal ceiling lower bound for every possible coupling, and comonotone quantiles attain it. Rescaling branch mass λ_i m gives a_i=1/λ_i and coefficient 1/Σλ_i².

At fixed normal the unit tangent chart preserves intrinsic length. Anchored compatibility gives actual membership and tightness fixes support height. Full physical convex tests restrict to one-dimensional convex tests and finite sums preserve their inequalities.
